events.title: Gosnold Sights Cape Cod
events.description: English explorer Bartholomew Gosnold became the first European recorded as seeing Cape Cod, off the coast of present-day Massachusetts. His expedition went on to explore the nearby coast and islands.
events.significance: The voyage added to early European knowledge of New England's coastline. That knowledge helped lead to English colonization of the region.

events.title: Virginia Calls for Independence
events.description: The Virginia Convention instructed its delegates to the Continental Congress to propose a declaration of independence from Great Britain.
events.significance: Virginia's instruction helped set in motion the resolution for independence. That resolution led to the Declaration of Independence in July 1776.

events.title: Birth of Pierre Curie
events.description: French physicist Pierre Curie was born in Paris. He later made important discoveries in magnetism and crystal physics. With his wife Marie, he pioneered research into radioactivity.
events.significance: The Curies shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Henri Becquerel for their work on radioactivity. Their research opened a new field of modern science.

events.title: Standard Oil Ordered Broken Up
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Standard Oil was an illegal monopoly under the Sherman Antitrust Act. It ordered the giant company dissolved into smaller, independent firms.
events.significance: The decision was a landmark in American antitrust law. It showed that even the nation's most powerful corporations could be broken up.

events.title: The First McDonald's Opens
events.description: Brothers Richard and Maurice McDonald opened a barbecue restaurant in San Bernardino, California. It was the first McDonald's. They later reworked it into a streamlined hamburger stand.
events.significance: The brothers' fast-service system became the model for the modern fast-food industry. The business grew into one of the world's best-known global brands.
